# Catalogue of claims

Author: Tsvetan Rouschev (ORCID 0009-0000-7312-9778). Licence: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0. Concept DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.22700098.

Every theorem the Lean kernel accepted is a product of this catalogue, and every product is claimed: 1846 products, 2 under a declared claim context and 1844 as the author's own statement, with 1495 variants (the examples a theorem names). 2 more are named by a sentence and not yet proved; they are listed at the end as claims still open.

The catalogue covers 20 standards, 7 with a theorem that states a fact the standard fixes and 13 open, and each of the 86 terms of ISO/IEC 4879:2024, every one with a theorem.

This catalogue records authorship and the date of each release. It is a publication, not a patent application: publishing a statement discloses it, and what is filed as a patent, and when, is for a patent attorney to decide before it is published.

### `Qpu.Verify.Stabilizer.conjCnotSigned_agrees_with_ruleCNOT`

Claimed by Tsvetan Rouschev as the author's own statement, by this name and as stated.

```lean
∀ (k : ℕ) (ct : Qpu.Verify.Stabilizer.P1 × Qpu.Verify.Stabilizer.P1),
  CircuitBasedQuantumComputing.ruleCNOT { k := k, x0 := ct.1.x, z0 := ct.1.z, x1 := ct.2.x, z1 := ct.2.z } =
    { k := (k + if (ct.1.x && ct.2.z && ct.2.x == ct.1.z) = true then 2 else 0) % 4, x0 := ct.1.x,
      z0 := ct.1.z ^^ ct.2.z, x1 := ct.1.x ^^ ct.2.x, z1 := ct.2.z }
```

    { k := (k + if (Qpu.Verify.Stabilizer.conjCnotSigned ct).1 = true then 2 else 0) % 4,
      x0 := (Qpu.Verify.Stabilizer.conjCnotSigned ct).2.1.x, z0 := (Qpu.Verify.Stabilizer.conjCnotSigned ct).2.1.z,
